title: Finding angles with a calculator
summary: Use the inverse trig keys in the right mode and find every angle that solves the equation.
objectives: Use sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ in degree and radian mode

lesson.md:
# Finding angles with a calculator

When a value is not in the special-angle table, the $\sin^{-1}$, $\cos^{-1}$ and $\tan^{-1}$ keys find an angle for you, but only **one** angle and only in a limited range. Your job is to check the mode and to find the other angles yourself.

lesson.title: Degree or radian mode?
lesson.md: Before you press anything, check the mode. $\sin^{-1}(0.5)$ is $30$ in degree mode and $0.5236$ in radian mode. Both are right, for different questions.

lesson.question: $\cos\theta=-0.4$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant III. Does $\cos^{-1}(-0.4)$ give you $\theta$?

options.why: $\cos^{-1}$ only returns angles from $0^\circ$ to $180^\circ$, so it can never land in Quadrant III.
It returns the Quadrant II angle, $113.6^\circ$. The Quadrant III angle is $180^\circ+66.4^\circ=246.4^\circ$.

steps.title: Reference angle
steps.md: Use the key on the **absolute value**: $\theta'=\sin^{-1}|v|$, and so on.

steps.title: Quadrants
steps.md: Decide which quadrants the sign allows (All Students Take Calculus).

steps.title: Build the angles
steps.md: Quadrant II: $180^\circ-\theta'$. Quadrant III: $180^\circ+\theta'$. Quadrant IV: $360^\circ-\theta'$.

lesson.title: $\sin\theta=-0.6$
lesson.problem: Solve $\sin\theta=-0.6$ for $0^\circ\le\theta<360^\circ$, to the nearest tenth of a degree.

steps.md: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV.

lesson.title: Two solutions of $\sin\theta=-0.6$
lesson.caption: The line $y=-0.6$ crosses one period of the sine wave twice.

lesson.md: Stopping at the calculator's answer. $\sin^{-1}(-0.6)\approx-36.9^\circ$ is not in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$, and it is only one of the two solutions.

points: Check degree or radian mode first.
The keys return one angle in a limited range.
Reference angle from $|v|$, then build every angle allowed by the sign.

prompt.md: Use a calculator to find the acute angle $\theta$ with $\sin\theta=0.75$, to the nearest tenth of a degree.

wrongs.why: Your calculator is in radian mode: $0.8481$ rad $\approx48.6^\circ$.

prompt.md: Find the acute angle $\theta$ with $\tan\theta=2.4$, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
Solve $\sin\theta=-0.6$ for $0^\circ\le\theta<360^\circ$, to the nearest tenth of a degree. Separate the answers with commas.

hints: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV.

wrongs.why: That is the calculator's answer, outside $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$ and only one of two solutions.
Those angles have a **positive** sine. Negative sine means Quadrants III and IV.

prompt.md: $\cos\theta=-0.4$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant III. Find $\theta$ to the nearest tenth of a degree.

wrongs.why: That is the Quadrant II angle that $\cos^{-1}$ returns. In Quadrant III use $180^\circ+\theta'$.

prompt.md: Find $\theta$ in radians, with $0\le\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, such that $\cos\theta=0.3$. Round to four decimals.

wrongs.why: Degree mode: the question asks for radians.

prompt.md: Which range of angles does $\tan^{-1}$ return?

options.why: Tangent is undefined at $\pm90^\circ$, so the interval is open.
Close, but $\tan^{-1}$ never reaches $\pm90^\circ$: tangent is undefined there.
No inverse key returns a whole turn: each gives one angle.

prompt.md: Solve $\tan\theta=-1.5$ for $0^\circ\le\theta<360^\circ$, to the nearest tenth of a degree. Separate the answers with commas.

hints: Tangent is negative in Quadrants II and IV.

prompt.md: True or false: in radian mode, $\sin^{-1}(0.5)$ is about $0.5236$.
A ramp rises $1.2$ m over a horizontal run of $9$ m. Find its angle of elevation, to the nearest tenth of a degree.

hints: Rise over run is the tangent.

wrongs.why: You used $\sin^{-1}$, but $9$ m is the horizontal run, not the length of the ramp: use $\tan^{-1}$.

prompt.md: Put the steps for solving $\cos\theta=-0.25$ on $[0^\circ, 360^\circ)$ in order.

items: Note that cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III

solution.md: Reference angle first, then the quadrants, then one angle per quadrant.

cards.front: First thing to check before using an inverse key
To solve $\sin\theta=v<0$ on $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$, use Quadrants {{c1::III}} and {{c2::IV}}.
Quadrant III angle from a reference angle $\theta'$
Quadrant IV angle from a reference angle $\theta'$
Angle of elevation from rise and run

mistakes.title: Wrong calculator mode
mistakes.why: The mode decides the unit of the answer.

mistakes.title: Only one solution
mistakes.why: Inverse keys return one angle; the sign usually allows two quadrants.
